The Hunt · art direction

Hand-drawn style lab

Same golfer, same range, same lighting: each finish is a post-process over the realistic render, so proportions and swing stay real. Frames are the portrait swing camera on a phone. More dots means the finish hides more of the procedural texture and modelling, so the art needs less detail to look good.

—

Realistic (today)

The game as it renders now: tone-mapped and graded, no illustration.

What it hides
Nothing. Every texture and modelling flaw shows.
How much simpler the art gets
1

Ink & Wash

Real lighting under a transparent watercolour wash, warm brown ink that thickens close to the camera, paper grain.

What it hides
Skin and fabric texture, small seams, turf tiling. The ink carries the shapes.
How much simpler the art gets
2

Painterly

Oil-paint brushwork across the frame with crisp ink edges kept on the golfer.

What it hides
Nearly all surface detail: cloth weave, hair strands, grass noise, tree cards.
How much simpler the art gets
3

Sports Poster

Soft-edged cel bands, bold navy outlines and halftone dots in the shadows.

What it hides
Texture detail and small shape errors; leans on clean silhouettes.
How much simpler the art gets
4

Gouache

Flat opaque paint, brush direction you can see, a warm palette and outlines tinted from the paint.

What it hides
Most texture and lighting noise. Faces become a few planes of colour.
How much simpler the art gets
5

Graphic Novel

Near-photoreal colour with cross-hatching in shadows and thin ink contours.

What it hides
Shadow noise and flat-looking cloth. Lit faces still show their detail.
How much simpler the art gets
